ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: icu

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Difficulty breathing, excessive salivation, and abdominal cramping

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He reports that he was spraying pesticides in his field earlier in the day when he began to feel ill. His wife notes that he has been sweating profusely and seems confused.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Tonsillectomy, age 8

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Hypertension, diagnosed age 65
- Mother: Hypothyroidism
- No family history of neurological disorders or psychiatric illness

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional (2-3 drinks per month). Occupation: Crop farmer and agricultural pesticide applicator.

VITAL SIGNS:
Respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute, heart rate is 110 beats per minute, blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, and temperature is 37.2°C (99°F)

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the patient is tachypneic with constricted pupils, diffuse muscle fasciculations, and wheezing on auscultation of the chest. His skin is moist and there is a garlic-like odor.

LABORATORY DATA:
Arterial blood gas shows a PaO2 of 60 mmHg, PaCO2 of 50 mmHg, and pH of 7.30.

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Suddenly collapsing

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to the emergency department approximately one year following a prior ICU admission for similar symptoms including difficulty breathing, excessive salivation, and abdominal cramping. He is brought by his brother after suddenly collapsing while working on a rural farm. Earlier in the day, he had been spraying the crops with a chemical pesticide without wearing protective equipment. According to his brother, the patient began complaining of dizziness, nausea, and difficulty seeing clearly. Within minutes, he developed excessive sweating, abdominal cramps, and vomiting. Shortly thereafter, he became confused, stumbled several times, and had a brief generalized convulsion that resolved spontaneously. Upon arrival at the hospital, the patient is lying on the gurney, drooling excessively and muttering incoherently. His clothes are damp with sweat, and he is visibly trembling. His breathing is shallow, and he intermittently coughs up small amounts of clear sputum. The patient’s brother says that no one else on the farm has had similar symptoms today. He adds that this particular pesticide had a “strong, bitter” smell, and that the patient accidentally spilled some on his shirt before continuing to work.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Organophosphate poisoning (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Tonsillectomy, age 8

MEDICATIONS:
He takes no medications

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Hypertension, diagnosed age 65
- Mother: Hypothyroidism
- No family history of neurological disorders or psychiatric illness

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional (2-3 drinks per month). Occupation: Crop farmer and agricultural pesticide applicator.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination reveals pinpoint pupils that respond sluggishly to light. His skin is cool and clammy, and muscle fasciculations are observed in both upper and lower extremities. Bowel sounds are hyperactive, and there is no abdominal distension or tenderness.
